messages.content: Help me execute the test runner `runThis` with arguments to set the wait time to 2 minutes and output the logs to a specific print stream `testLogStream`, considering the debuggee name is 'TestDebuggee'?

function.name: runThis
function.description: Executes the test runner with provided arguments and a print stream for logging. It handles the debuggee binding, output redirection, and test execution flow. Note that the provided function is in Java 8 SDK syntax.

argv.description: An array of strings representing the command-line arguments, to include waittime and debuggeeName. Format: -waitTime, <waitTime>, -debuggeeName, TestDebuggee This is Java Array type parameter in string representation. The list elements are of type String; they are not in string representation.

out.description: The PrintStream to output the logs to. This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation.

message.reasoning:
The user wants us to call the tool "runThis" from the namespace "functions". We need to provide an argument structure:

{
 argv: ...,
 out: ...
}

We have to pass the correct format.

They want to set wait time to 2 minutes (120 seconds). Waittime param expects integer? They said "-waitTime, <waitTime>" so we should supply as string maybe "120"? Or "2m"? But likely numeric value in seconds or milliseconds. We'll assume it's number of seconds. So use "120".

Also debuggeeName param: "-debuggeeName", "TestDebuggee"

So argv would be something like ["-waitTime","120","-debuggeeName","TestDebuggee"]

But note the description says "An array of strings representing the command-line arguments, to include waittime and debuggeeName." So yes.

Now out: "testLogStream" which presumably refers to some PrintStream instance variable named testLogStream. In code they'd refer to it directly. For our JSON, we just put the reference string "testLogStream".

Thus produce JSON:

{
   "argv": [
      "-waitTime",
      "120",
      "-debuggeeName",
      "TestDebuggee"
   ],
   "out": "testLogStream"
}

Return this via calling the tool.
